oncall-bot: PAGING — p99 decode latency spike on prod-gpu-cluster-3, triggered alert at 2026-09-04T15:20:34Z. Current p99 ~ 1.4s (SLO 700ms). Auto-notify to #eng-oncall :rotating_light:

Sara: saw it — thanks. I'm on call. any deploys in last 30m?

mike: yes, infra-team pushed a kernel+linker roll (kernel v5.12-rtlink-2026.09) 12m ago to the TRT nodes, also a FlashAttention libc bump on the image. Noted increased tail on streaming.

rita: customer-facing metrics show elevated streaming stalls; p95 steady at 350ms but p99 jumping. A subset of requests time out at 2s and get retried, causing retries to cascade.

Sara: ok let's triage quickly. dan, can you confirm if decode path got a new kernel ABI flag or LTO?

Dan: yes — build pipeline added -flto and linker script change to enable fastmem mapping for flash kernels. It was intended to reduce memory copies but may change instruction alignment for fused kernels.

Paul: Support reports 3 high-sev incidents from customers using streaming chat (dedicated and hosted). They started around 15:18 UTC. Customer impact: increased latency causing stalled streams; some clients saw partial tokens then long silence.

mike: pulling live perf traces now. Initial flame graphs show decode kernel spends more time in memcpy and cache-miss hotspots after the linker change; KV cache hit patterns look normal.

Sara: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) Rollback kernel/linker image to previous build on a small canary pool 2) Disable LTO/linker optimization, rebuild quickly 3) Route critical traffic to fallback model variant on older image 4) Increase streaming request timeout/backoff to avoid retries. Which can we do fast?

Dan: fastest is to route traffic away from nodes running the new image. We can change routing policy to prefer pool A (older image) within 2-3 minutes. Rollback of nodes takes longer (drain + redeploy).

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline activity detected: rollback option queued. Use `/deploy status image-2026-09-04` to inspect.

rita: I'll start routing change and monitor p99 in real time. Sara, can you coordinate with Mike to validate traces after routing change?

Sara: yes. Doing routing change now — switching 40% of traffic off cluster-3 onto cluster-1/2 (previous image).

mike: tracing after route shift: p99 dropped to ~820ms within 90s, p95 unchanged. Streaming stalls rate reduced by ~70%.

Paul: telling affected customers we have a mitigation in place and are working towards full rollback.

Dan: we've reproduced locally: the linker reorder plus `-flto` caused hot loop to be emitted with extra spill instructions on Ampere GPUs under TRT fused kernels -> more DRAM traffic. FlashAttention libc expects tight alignment; small misalignments increase cache-line thrash.

Sara: plan: 1) keep routing to older image until we have a safe patched image 2) patch build: disable LTO and revert linker script change, run smoke perf tests 3) run canary deploy to 5% then ramp 4) postmortem & notify customers

rita: making incident page: https://infra.internal/incidents/1768501234 (adding notes & timelines).

mike: patch build in progress. quick perf test command we used locally:
```bash
./bench_decode --model t5-large --seq 1024 --batch 1 --trials 200 --trace flamegraph > trace.out
```
Flame shows memcpy spikes at decode_loop+0x1f4 and unexpected L2 misses.

Dan: small repro snippet showing padded alignment difference: 
```c
// before
__attribute__((aligned(64))) float fused_buf[...];
// after linker reorder
float fused_buf[...] ; // lost alignment in emitted section
```
This explains misaligned loads under vectorized kernels.

Sara: ETA for patched image?

Dan: if we skip LTO and revert linker change, we can produce an image in ~25 minutes; canary deploy + smoke tests 15 more. So ~45-50 mins to full ramp if green.

Sara: ok, do it. Rita, keep monitoring. Mike, when can you validate end-to-end streaming for customer workloads?

mike: I'll run the customer workload replay on canary once deploy hits 5% — should be able to validate within 10 minutes of canary start.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for image-2026-09-04-patch at 2026-09-04T15:44:10Z, target 5% (pool A).

rita: metrics update: p99 fell to 540ms on canary nodes, global p99 now 600ms and trending down. Incidents open reduced to 1 (ongoing for a single tenant still hitting tails).

Paul: support asked for ETA to tell customer: say ~1 hour for full remediation, we're currently in canary and will ramp if green.

Sara: briefing for handoff in 30 mins: summary, mitigation steps, root-cause hypothesis (linker + LTO causing misalignment and cache thrash on fused TRT/FlashAttention kernels), and next steps (full patch roll, postmortem).

Dan: note for postmortem: add test-case in CI that runs fused-kernel alignment checks under both LTO and non-LTO builds; add alignment asserts to FlashAttention integration tests.

mike: also recommend adding a perf-smoke gate on canary for p99 decode > 800ms to block rollouts.

Sara: agreed. I'll add that to rollout checklist.

rita: switching to oncall-handoff: @oncall-next please pick up in 30m, we'll include timelines in incident page.

oncall-bot: HANDOFF scheduled to 2026-09-04T16:20:00Z for next oncall rotation.

Paul: I'll prepare customer-facing blurb and add it to the incident page.

Sara: thanks all. Current status: mitigation in place (traffic steer), canary showing restored SLOs, patch build validated. Continue monitoring; we'll update page and do a full rollback only if canary fails.

mike: leaving traces and perf dumps in /var/tmp/incident-1768501234/ for postmortem.

rita: closing page note with timeline. Last check 15:46:00Z p99=580ms.

Sara: handing off to next oncall at 16:20. If any regression while I'm out, escalate to runtime lead. :thumbsup:
